name: Burggraf von Rietenburg
credit: Burggraf von Rietenburg, miniature in the Codex Manesse (Heidelberg, Cod. Pal. germ. 848), c. 1300–1340 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: The Burggraf von Rietenburg is one of the earliest named German minnesingers, a nobleman of the Bavarian Danube region in the second half of the twelfth century, of whom only a few strophes survive.
One of his songs appears here in Frank C. Nicholson’s translation, Old German Love Songs (1907), made from the minnesingers of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

poems.title: I shall come forth as Gold
poems.author: Burggraf von Rietenburg
poems.text:
This above all wealth I hold,
That to prove me's her desire.
I shall then be found like gold
Which is tested in the fire
And right well assayed.
All the better thus 'tis made,
Brighter, purer, fairer too.
What my song declares, is true.
The hotter it doth glow,
All the fairer will it show.
